What degraded

  • The deck shipped UNDER the bar at 6.762 against 6.8, 0.038 short. No judge found a hard fail, the panel had reached the five round cap where the routine's own rule is that the deck ships at its honest median rather than being reworked, and carousel no. 13 shipped at 6.562 the day before. The heaviest criterion, artwork craft at 0.28 of the weight, scored 6.8 and is the work the next run inherits.
  • The light deck cap was WAIVED by name for this date, on the owner's instruction. This deck measures deck median L* 73.1 against a threshold of 60.0, and it is the second light deck inside the counted eight run window against brand.yaml's cap of one. The cap was not raised and the count is still measured off the render and still printed on every run.
  • The lightness was NOT the deliberate high variance move brand.yaml permits. The storyboard planned a median near 43 and nobody measured until round 3, so the rule was broken by a plan never checked against its own render. The next deck is required dark and artwork.json's avoid_next now says so first.
  • The Supabase connector was unavailable for the second consecutive day, so the scanner's daily cap query did not run. Nobody is notified about a ceiling nobody is notified about.
  • Two decisions rest on sources no client here can read. tx-2026-0038 moved to the board's own minutes and tx-2026-0098 to the NSF award record, and one sentence was dropped rather than carried from a page that cannot be re-read.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Who gets an invitation, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Who gets an invitation?

The Texas A&M University System's VISION supercomputer ranked No. 66 in the world at 34.82 petaflops measured. It sits in the West Campus Data Center at Texas A&M University.

VISION's own documentation states the present condition. Access is invitation-only and approved via TAMUS governance. The current status is controlled beta.

Two System pages describe who VISION is for. Both use the future tense. One reads "VISION will be available to researchers of all disciplines across the entire Texas A&M System".

Onboarding is expected to begin with the institutions that finished integration, and the front page is seeking beta testers. The documentation states the access rule and states no number. How many researchers can use it today?

#TexasAMSystem #VISIONsupercomputer #TOP500

What this deck does not say, because the sources do not.

TOP500 publishes no university category. Neither its list page nor its system detail page calls
VISION the fastest university supercomputer in the United States. That framing belongs to the
System and to Tarleton State, and VISION's own site says only that it is one of the
highest-performing AI supercomputers at any North American university.

No page fetched names a county or a city for the West Campus Data Center, so this record names
none.

No dated Board of Regents action was found. The newsroom states the approval and gives no
meeting date and no agenda item.

The compound counts are printed as their own sources wrote them and are never joined. Nothing
in the record connects them, and about a week is not a duration this record can turn into a rate.

The full entry, with every claim and every source, is on the record at texasaidocket.com

The machine changed itself

  • The always-sent ask index rolls the data centre dossier family up, grouped by county, instead of giving 150 facilities a full line each
    The index went 450 characters over its 40,000 ceiling, which is the block every question pays for. The run escalated it as out of its lane and its measurement of the bulk was wrong, naming reservoirs at 39 percent when they are 8. The dossiers were the one family still indexed line by line. 12,403 characters became 9,436 and the index sits at 36,963
  • A named, dated waiver mechanism for the light deck cap, with a self-test proving a third light deck still fails
    The owner waived the cap for one deck. Raising LIGHT_CAP would have permitted every future second light deck, and editing artwork.json to hide the measurement would corrupt the memory the cap is counted from. The waiver names one date, expires on its own, and never stops the count
  • The record's shape is recorded at version 2
    geography.on_ercot widened from bool to bool or null, because a federal derivatives docket is neither on the ERCOT grid nor off it and false was a confident answer to a question that does not apply. The run raised SPEC_VERSION and stopped, correctly, because the contract is human owned
  • No routine writes a worklog, at any path
    The host classes everything under .claude/ as a sensitive file and prompts on every edit whatever the permission mode says, which stopped five unattended runs. run_state.json already carried the resume state

Each reverts on its own commit.

Notes

The record woke in good shape for the first time this week, because the September 2nd run cleared all 98 items. 6 due, 0 rotten, 0 deferred. All six were worked by hand and the ledger went from 98 items to 103 and from 517 claims to 549. Five decisions were admitted, each with a primary source and each naming where it is. Austin City Council starting land code amendments for data centre use, a Dallas Public Safety Committee briefing on the police Flock program, a UT Austin course AI policy required in every syllabus, a federal comment window open to October 20th on compute derivatives, and the Texas A&M System's VISION supercomputer, which is this deck's own story and was admitted so the carousel is built on a decision the record holds. Two scout findings were dropped rather than admitted. A Katy ISD framework whose headline quote turned out to be two sentences merged with the full stop removed, and a Pflugerville Flock non-renewal resting on journalism alone. Two items were resting on documents that cannot be re-read and both were moved to sources that can. The share of claims resting on a primary document went UP rather than down. The backlog is three, unchanged, all three grandfathered ERCOT items that predate the geography rule. It did not grow.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
